Per the project's recorded release convention (the only source I found; there's no release doc or CI config in the repo):

1. **Pick the version** as `vYYYY.MM.N`. `N` is the running release count within that month. Today is 2026-10-01, so the first release this month would be `v2026.10.1`. The example in the memory is `v2026.09.2`.
2. **Tag and push it**, for example `git tag v2026.10.1 && git push origin v2026.10.1`. Tag the commit you want released, normally a clean `main`.
3. **Let CI do the rest.** CI builds and publishes on the tag push. Never publish by hand.

I didn't find CI workflow files, so I can't tell you what CI checks or whether it needs a release branch or changelog. I also can't tell how `N` is counted, for example whether it resets each month. If you want, I can check existing git tags to confirm the numbering.
